candidate_sentences.text: Total revenue increased by 14.4% to EUR 216.6 million, compared with EUR 189.3 million in the previous year, driven primarily by higher interest revenue and increased fee and commission income related to financing activities.

Profitability improved significantly, with net profit before foreign exchange results rising by 14.9% to EUR 32.5 million, and total net profit reaching EUR 29.6 million, representing a 21.0% increase compared with EUR 24.5 million reported in the previous year.
The company achieved an all-time high adjusted EBITDA of EUR 89.8 million, up from EUR 77.5 million in the prior year.
The net portfolio of vehicle and consumer financing grew by 15.9% to EUR 371.2 million at the end of the period, compared with EUR 320.3 million a year earlier.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key year-over-year improvements included a 29.3% capitalization ratio (vs 26.1% in 2023), 2.4 interest coverage ratio (vs 2.3), and reduced net leverage to 3.3x (from 3.7x).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report financial highlights; Note 48 Alternative Performance Measures

candidate_sentences.text: Total equity increased to EUR 108.1 million as of December 31, 2024, compared with EUR 65.4 million at the end of the previous period, resulting in a stronger capitalization ratio of 29.3%.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major performance drivers were organic growth in Europe/Africa, successful integration of Sub-Saharan operations (tripling regional portfolio), digital transformation (doubled applications, new self-service platform), and enhanced risk management improving portfolio quality.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO keynote; Management report operations section

candidate_sentences.text: The financial results were supported by steady macroeconomic conditions in core regions, stable operational execution, and the successful integration of previously acquired operations, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa.

verified_key_information_units.information: Business segments showed vehicle finance (67% of portfolio: 45% traditional, 20% flexible/subscription) and consumer finance (33%: Kredo, Tigo, etc.), with key growth in East Africa (e-motorcycles), Romania, Uganda, and Albania offsetting exits from Balkan/Belarus.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report segments; Sustainability statement portfolio balance; Note 19 discontinued operations

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital structure transformed via October 2024 IPO raising EUR 29.0 mln equity (largest in Nasdaq Riga history), used to repay subordinated bonds and high-cost Mintos loans, while expanding local currency funding (Kenya +30%, Botswana notes).

candidate_sentences.text: A major strategic development during the reporting period was the successful initial public offering of the company in October, which raised EUR 29.0 million in equity proceeds and strengthened its capital position while expanding its presence on public capital markets.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic priorities include deepening existing markets, broadening product portfolio (e.g., electric motorcycle financing surpassing 2025 targets), geographic expansion, and developing ESG strategy for 2026-2031 with climate neutrality targets for HQ operations.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, and K5 are PRESENT with clear evidence in the candidate summary. K3 is PARTIALLY_PRESENT as it mentions successful integration of Sub-Saharan operations but omits other core drivers (organic growth in Europe/Africa, digital transformation, enhanced risk management). K4, K6, and K7 are MISSING entirely - no details on business segment structure, strategic priorities, or post-reporting period events appear in the candidate text. The summary captures the strongest financial metrics and IPO but lacks strategic depth and forward-looking elements required for full coverage.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of strong financial performance. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. Each sentence builds upon the previous ones, providing a clear progression of financial highlights, performance metrics, strategic developments, and overall conclusions without any internal inconsistencies. The financial figures are presented consistently, and the adjustments (e.g., one-off tax expense) are clearly explained without creating contradictions. The summary forms a coherent whole that aligns with the introductory and concluding statements.
